newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends down sharply in correction.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends down sharply in correction.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices pulled back more than six cents on Thursday as speculators took profits one day after the market surged to its highest level in nearly two and a half years, traders said.
Prices drifted on either side of unchanged for much of the session, but the market spiralled sharply lower toward the day's end amid heavy long liquidation.

Traders said the sell-off was all but inevitable following the market's stunning rise. Coffee prices, which have gained more than 50 percent since the start of the year, had climbed more than 15 percent in the last week alone before selling off today.
May arabica futures slumped 6.95 cents per lb, to close near the day's lows at 193.70 cents. Trades were posted from 193.25 to 205. July futures fell 6.05, to 181.15
"No matter how bullish the funds are, at times profit-taking sets in and you have a correction," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "The market just needed to take a breather."

Talk that Colombia would open registrations for April-June coffee shipments may have exacerbated the slide, dealers said. After the close of trading, Colombian coffee officials confirmed April-June registrations for private exporters would be opened on Friday, March 7.

In addition to the 1.07 million bags of new excelso coffee it authorized for shipment, the National Growers' Federation indicated it might approve the sale of 300,000 bags of old coffee during the same time period.
With much of today's losses occurring late in the session, dealers said the market would likely continue to work its way lower on Friday.
"This is the first time in a while the market finished at the lows of the day, so chances are we will see follow-through selling," a trader said.
Next support was seen at 182 cents, followed by 177. Resistance was noted at 195 cents, and then at 200 and 210.
The day's volume was estimated at 15,660 lots, versus 18,998 lots on Wednesday. ((-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
